layers.note: A shrub of subalpine meadow edges, tree clumps, avalanche tracks and open woods.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; often cool slopes and clump edges.

elevation_m.note: Low elevations in Alaska; about 1,030 to 2,030 m in Montana (FEIS, Matthews 1993); subalpine in the Washington Cascades.

shade_tolerance.note: Sun to part shade; flowers and fruits best in the open.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −15 to 3 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 7 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −38 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −45 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 8 to 18 °C; gone below 6 °C, where summers are too short, and above 22 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 700 to 3,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 400.

degree_days_5.note: About 200 to 1,800 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 80.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.55, gone by 0.4.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.5 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.7.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Sitka mountain-ash grows from Alaska south along the Pacific Coast and through the Cascade Range to northern California and east to northern Idaho and northwestern Montana (FEIS, Matthews 1993, for the species as then circumscribed). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
